The former unrestricted preparation wrappers are absent from the final proof. The concrete screen consistency proof and one-frame construction remain unadopted simplifications.

October 31: integrate concrete linear predictor consistency into the final zero-discrepancy preparation. Collect actual joint frequencies, apply the prepared endpoint rank estimate before restrictions, recenter a finite affine-probe array in one random common cell using only Z, retain fixed ticket density bounds, and derive an odd-tag prediction-error contradiction. The old synthetic-distribution consistency and unary slice comparison are absent. The graph statement is unchanged; one-frame quadratic construction and reduced mixers remain unadopted.

October 31: prove one-frame laws and exact-image bounds, cycle quadratic annihilator decomposition, bounded-rank selected-cut channel realization for one endpoint, frozen frame completion with exact kernel, and independent reciprocal channel blocks. These new results are audited auxiliary proofs; joint endpoint/collision assembly, new-law phase/query estimates, reduced mixers and final adoption remain unfinished.

Complete and adopt the actual one-frame quadratic construction: closed-pin preparation, phase alternative, quadratic-Gram retained-column high moments, linear all-filter partitions and predictor consistency, both scalar contradictions, and matching exposure. The unchanged graph theorem now uses OneConstruction.exists_graphs. The reduced mixer family remains separate work; the manuscript remains the historical exposition checkpoint.

Integrate the reduced Jg-pair mixer family into the single-frame final producer. Prove its unary random-rank estimate and explicit binary rank bound, expand canonical prescription bits, and rebuild both scalar alternatives and the unchanged graph theorem. All construction simplifications are now adopted; conservative finite rank budgets and deferred scalar ultrafilters remain. The natural-language manuscript is still the historical exposition checkpoint.

November 1: rewrite the complete manuscript around the integrated odd-cycle, single quadratic-frame construction with reduced mixers and linear key partitions. Include the joint endpoint kernel repair, the full-image-kernel polynomial in the capped-leaf Fourier estimate, the concrete coherent-array predictor argument, and linear-cell predicted overlap. Retain the original graph theorem. Compile to 55 pages at the existing type size and margins; the Lean sources are unchanged from 6738184.

November 4: adopt exact common quadratic predictions fitted at accuracy 1/1000, literal finite prediction classes and zero prediction error. Replace majority trace consistency and true-intersection truncation by tester support and initial pin rank, choosing g = 4e + 20001 after the early budgets. Replace relative quadratic extension by linear constraints and coordinate matrix factorization. Replace predicted superlevel overlap by relative cell hits, a weighted cell sum and one clipping estimate. Rewrite the corresponding manuscript sections; the compiled text remains 55 pages. The outer asymptotic ultrafilter remains. All changes use the original graph statement.

November 5: integrate direct even moments with auxiliary dual-vector kernel certificates and exact status supports. Full linear fibers give a uniform support gap; exact scalar relations and seven canonical predictor pairs replace majority extraction and the 128-choice dictionary. Exact quadratic sections replace fixed-accuracy fitting in both preparation alternatives. The four-corner and image-kernel-sieve routes are absent from the final proof. The manuscript is 56 pages; label-span stabilization, table surrogates, shared query laws and finite outer preparation remain.

November 8: replace repeated-hit bounds in the partition energy and clipping certificate by a multirow frame count, a whole-query rank-deficit bound, and bounded L1 approximation. Orbit averaging proves the row count with constant 2^(d^2+2); d is fixed before partition complexity. The actual input density caps discharge the uniform-input comparison. The final proof uses this route and excludes the repeated-hit theorems. The original graph statements are unchanged.

November 8: replace repeated label-span stabilization by exact polynomial continuation for arbitrary edge linear relations. Prove that positive reference colors have positive empirical mass on the prepared rank event, so all-input identities imply conditional support identities. The original graph theorem uses the unchanged seven-generator bound directly on the original spans. The old stabilization search is absent. Conservative finite exclusion parameters are retained; the common good-event row bound changes from 2gR to 3gR. Support surrogates, generic-only query laws and finite outer preparation remain.

November 8: replace full-status probability-table surrogates by support indicators with a fixed status-atom lower bound. Numerical scores use support intersections, and positive product tests give one-sided projected domination. The final score calendar preserves independent leaves and pair-dependent filters. Direct base-query comparison removes the remaining expansion over internal-bit assignments. Final proof-term and axiom audits pass; shared query laws and finite outer preparation remain.

November 9: exact predictions and scalar witnesses use generic inputs; shared identities follow by setting ordinary coordinates to zero. Replace the final ultrafilter preparation by finite cofinal restrictions, preserving the unchanged graph statement. The shared analytic query family and a fully finite preparation theorem remain pending.

November 9: restrict concentration, common-score comparison and both witness branches to generic queries. Preserve independently sampled leaves and pair-dependent filters. Both preparation branches retain a fixed positive mass, using an explicit finite trimming inequality; the general subexponential trimming theorem is absent. The all-flavor table representation and fully finite outer assembly remain pending.

Use a basis of light rows to bound the support of a matrix with nonzero diagonal. Apply the bound to both phase relations and carry inverse-square compatibility through prediction and collision. Count new columns by translating a quadratic character. The same formula supplies independent columns and full ambient frame symmetry.

Use one positive preparation quota at every sufficiently large dimension for every admissible law. Test all attained predictor cells on both diagonal slices. Ambient rank gives reciprocal zero compatibility and, with the singleton character bound, a fourth-power bound on the prescribed four bits. The direct estimate on accepted cell masses enters the predicted branch. Separate two-position results treat all binary and unary prescriptions at feasible keys.

Replace geometric mark records by the offset and two restricted functionals. Count four zero readings directly on their span. Recover full accepted key fibers at every valid frame. Construct a law on actual frames satisfying every image-spreading bound at arbitrarily small exponential allowances for which independent draws have zero overlap for every complete option.

Give both prescribed-one phase masks a rank alternative. Bound the mass of nonzero marked offsets in a fixed space from the prepared endpoint laws and use it in finite preparation. Obtain complete-key cuts from the collision estimate. Count Gram constraints for a fixed number of pooled queries to handle tests of both endpoints supplied by the opposite leaf. The general phase and overlap replacements remain open.

Select the large Fourier coefficients for all filters on a capped leaf using Parseval. A basis of frequent characters captures the intersections of the two original leaf spaces. Replace the greedy tensor exposure by one minimum over finite subsets. All estimates retain the independent leaf draws and the original cap and rank bounds.
